title: China's 15th Five-Year Plan
summary: The 2026–2030 national plan that sets China's science and industrial priorities.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

The Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee, meeting in October 2025, adopted recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, which governs 2026 to 2030. The text elevates 'self-reliance and strength in science and technology' and the construction of a modern industrial system, with advanced manufacturing, AI and energy security as recurring themes. Five-year plans are directional rather than binding budgets, but they align ministries, banks and state-owned buyers behind a small number of priorities.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Mass production
Estimated window 2026–2030
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

  • China Big Fund III
  • China's embodied AI initiative

Investment Exposure

The plan matters commercially because it tells you where subsidised capacity will appear over the next five years, which is usually where prices fall fastest.

What Would Change The View

  • Whether implementation details attach hard funding targets.
  • Which provinces are named as pilot zones.
  • How foreign participation is treated in the final outline.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
